name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write

27: helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.

32: ## Shell timing
33: 
34: When writing shell scripts,
35: always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
36: Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
37: the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
38: slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
39: interactive shell commands.
40: 
41: ## Ideas
42: 
43: Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
44: `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
45: `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.
46: 
47: 
48: 
49: 
50: ## Links in handoffs
51: 
52: When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
53: link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
54: requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
55: than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
56: the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.
57: 
58: When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.
59: 
60: ## OpenCode GitHub Actions
61: 
62: To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
63: Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
64: The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
65: verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.
66: 
67: When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
68: Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
69: logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
70: for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
71: which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.
72: 
73: Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
74: Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
75: Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
76: Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
77: Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.
78: 
79: Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
80: Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.
81: 
82: To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
83: `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
84: then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
85: with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.
86: 
87: When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
88: over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
89: same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
90: is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
91: live log evidence can be collected.
92: 
93: For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:
94: 
95: ```sh
96: bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
97: ```
98: 
99: The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
100: request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
101: `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
102: inspecting the runner.
103: 
104: ## Mac SSH access
105: 
106: The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
107: stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
108: commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:
109: 
110: ```sh
111: ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
112: ```
113: 
114: The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.
115: 
116: ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker
117: 
118: Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
119: or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:
120: 
121: ```sh
122: bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
123: ```
124: 
125: For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
126: use the same key:
127: 
128: ```sh
129: ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
130:   -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
131:   -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
132:   -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
133: ```
134: 
135: Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
136: can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
137: worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
138: print secrets while inspecting a worker.

## Objective
- Build a polished 2D Breakout game where the ball splits on every hit, likely as a browser game in this repo.
- Deliver a visually strong, responsive game playable on desktop and mobile, with screenshot-capture compatibility.

## Requirements
- User request: “2D Breakout where the ball splits on every hit”.
- Must support mobile and desktop, responsive layout, touch controls, and safe areas.
- Use browser verification/screenshots.
- No explicit requirements beyond the user prompt and repository guidance.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained static HTML/CSS/JS game, no framework.
- Named the game “SPLIT/BREAK”; split occurs on brick and paddle impacts, capped at 14 balls.
- Implemented levels, scores, combo multipliers, 3 lives, local best score, synth WebAudio, particles, screen shake, pause/game-over screens.
- Replaced expensive visuals for software-rendering performance:
  - Removed SVG grain and scanline overlays.
  - Removed large CSS blur/filter/mix-blend effects.
  - Switched from per-brick canvas sprites to grouped `Path2D` row rendering.
  - Added software renderer detection and `RENDER_SCALE = 0.62`.
  - Currently canvas context is `{ alpha: false }` with flat background fill.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css`, `game.js` implemented with full game logic and UI.
- Gameplay includes brick splitting, impacts, paddle physics, levels, particles, sounds, HUD, overlays, touch/keyboard input.
- Initial capture succeeded and confirmed both desktop and mobile layouts render.
- Identified and mostly removed several severe SwiftShader/llvmpipe performance bottlenecks.
- Verified game page loads without syntax errors after latest changes.

### Active
- Performance optimization for software-rendered desktop screenshots.
- Current desktop FPS is ~10 FPS while mobile is much faster/60 FPS.
- Discovered blocking CSS is the cause: with `styles.css` aborted, performance is 60 FPS; with CSS loaded, ~10 FPS.
- Need isolate which CSS rule/section causes the remaining 60→10 FPS degradation.

### Blocked
- Playwright auto-start on desktop sometimes struggles because of low initial FPS/stability.
- Screenshot capture must reliably show gameplay, not only the intro title.

## Next Move
1. Bisect `styles.css` while JS runs to find the exact rule causing 60→10 FPS. Previous section tests implicated intro CSS, but individual overrides did not consistently fix it.
2. Remove or simplify the culprit rule, likely a full-screen compositing/gradient/transform effect in intro/topbar/app background.
3. Re-enable a richer background if possible, since current opaque canvas hides CSS ambience; consider restoring `alpha: true` with `clearRect` after CSS is fixed.
4. Verify desktop >20 FPS and mobile near 60.
5. Re-run capture:
   ```sh
   CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002/ CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots bash capture.sh
   ```
6. Inspect `screenshots/final-desktop.png` and `screenshots/final-mobile.png`.
7. Remove temporary debug globals/flags:
   - `window.__splitDebug`
   - `window.__splitRender`
   - `window.__splitLayers`
   - `window.__lastFrameWork`
   - unused `makeBrickGradient`, `makeBrickSprite`, `rebuildBrickLayer`, `ensureBrickLayer`, unused `bgGradient/topGlow/bottomGlow` references if appropriate.
8. Run `node --check game.js`.
9. Optionally add an automation-only auto-start (`navigator.webdriver`) if capture still fails despite adequate FPS, but avoid affecting normal users.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: main game logic, physics, rendering, temporary debug hooks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game UI, canvas, overlays, controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: layout/visual design; current performance bottleneck.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/final-desktop.png`: latest desktop capture (intro screen from earlier run).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/final-mobile.png`: latest mobile capture (gameplay).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: starts runtime static server via `default-start.mjs`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: runs runtime Playwright capture.

## Important Context
- Server is running on `http://localhost:3002` via background shell.
- Browser renderer is `ANGLE (Mesa, Vulkan 1.4.335 (llvmpipe ...))` — software rendering despite runtime docs mentioning SwiftShader.
- Test helpers exist:
  - `/tmp/opencode/fps.js`
  - `/tmp/opencode/fpstime.js`
  - `/tmp/opencode/fpslayers3.js`
  - `/tmp/opencode/fpscssjs.js`
  - `/tmp/opencode/fpsintro.js`
- Key FPS findings:
  - With CSS loaded and JS rendering: ~10 FPS desktop.
  - With `styles.css` blocked: ~60 FPS desktop.
  - With rendering disabled: ~60 FPS.
  - Rendering work measured at only ~0.2ms JS time; GPU/compositor raster is the bottleneck.
- JS now uses `Path2D` row batching for bricks, but performance remained ~9–10 FPS because CSS causes most of the cost.
- Current canvas:
  - Context: `alpha: false`
  - Render scale: `RENDER_SCALE = 0.62` on software renderer
  - Render uses flat `#05060d` fill.
- `game.js` still contains unused sprite/layer code and temporary debug globals.
- Capture currently logs no JS errors after fixing missing `rebuildBrickLayer`; however current code needs final re-verification.
- Worktree is uncommitted; no git commit/push made.
